info.title: Dataverse Web API (admin subset)
info.description:
The Dataverse Web API is the OData v4 interface each environment exposes at its own organization host. This spec covers the **administration and ALM subset** — table and record operations, solutions and solution import, environment variables, publishers, users, security roles and organization settings — not business data.

Each environment publishes its own complete, authoritative model at `/api/data/v9.2/$metadata` (CSDL); consult it for tables and columns specific to an environment.

Responses follow OData conventions: `@odata.context`, `@odata.etag`, `_field_value` for lookups, an `OData-EntityId` header on creates, and `@odata.nextLink` for paging. Errors are `{"error":{"code","message"}}` with hexadecimal codes.

The separate **Discovery** service resolves which organizations a user can reach, and their Web API URLs.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/dataverse) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

x-notes.note:
**Routes found on this API and deliberately left out, with the reason.** This spec is a curated admin and ALM subset; the tables below are real and reachable, and belong to other products that happen to store their data in Dataverse. Recorded so nobody re-discovers them and assumes an oversight.

**Finance and Operations provisioning** -- `msprov_getfnoversiondetails`, `msprov_queuefnoinstallorupdate`, `msprov_operationhistories` (and its `msprov_logs/$value` attachment stream), `msprov_getfinopsapplicationdetails`, `msprov_getfinopssqljitaccessasync`, `msprov_fnopackages`, `msprov_fnomodules`, `RetrieveFinanceAndOperationsIntegrationDetails`, `mserp_financeandoperationsentities`. A distinct product surface with its own lifecycle. Note that `msprov_getfinopssqljitaccessasync` returns live database credentials, so a client enumerating custom actions should not call it casually.

**Power Pages tables** -- `powerpagesites`, `mspp_webroles`. The management API for Power Pages is on the Power Platform API host and is documented in the `ppapi` spec; these are its storage.

**Copilot Studio and AI Builder** -- `bots`, `bots({id})/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.PvaDeleteBot`, `msdyn_aimodels`. Bots are administered through the Copilot Studio host, which has its own spec here.

**SOAP** -- `POST /XRMServices/2011/Organization.svc/web`. Out of scope by the same rule that keeps the regional discovery endpoints out: this spec covers the REST Web API.

Every one of these was observed in a working third-party administration tool, so their absence is a scope decision rather than a coverage gap.

servers.description: The environment's own Dataverse host. Resolve it from the admin APIs; it is not derivable from an environment id.

tags.name: Batch
tags.description: Multiple Web API requests sent as one `multipart/mixed` document. The mechanism by which a client groups reads, or makes a set of writes atomic through a change set.

tags.name: Dataverse Search
tags.description: The environment's search index: whether it has been provisioned, and whether Customer Lockbox gates it. Enabling search is an admin-centre operation; this reports the result.

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description:
Which Dataverse organizations does this token's user have access to, and what is each one's Web API URL?

This is the boundary that turns an identity into a set of environment hosts. It matters because the rest of this spec has nowhere to start without it: the Web API's host is per environment and **not derivable from an environment id**, so a caller either learns it from the admin APIs ([bapi](spec:bapi), [ppapi](spec:ppapi)) or learns it here. Discovery is the route that needs no admin permission and no environment id — just a token.

It is a separate service on its own hosts, with its own audience and its own OData model. It is not part of any environment's `$metadata`, and an environment's token is not accepted by it.

**Service principals are not admitted.** App-only identities have no access to the Global Discovery Service: a request carrying one is refused with a 401. Plan for app-only clients to discover environments through BAPI instead.

## Global versus regional discovery

There are two generations of discovery service, and they are easy to confuse.

- **Global discovery**, documented here, is the OData v4 service at `https://globaldisco.{cloud}/api/discovery/v2.0/`. It answers for every region at once, and it is what a modern client should use.
- **Regional discovery** is the older per-region SOAP endpoint at `https://disco.crm{n}.dynamics.com/XRMServices/2011/Discovery.svc`. It is out of scope for this spec — it is SOAP, not OData — but its region-to-host mapping is what ties a CRM region number to a geography, so it is reproduced in full below.

Three regions that otherwise require regional discovery have their own global discovery host and are reached through that instead: China, US Gov High and US Gov DoD, plus the North America 2 scale group. Germany (the sovereign `microsoftdynamics.de` cloud) requires regional discovery and has **no** global discovery host, so global discovery cannot reach it at all.

## Region map

| GER | GER | Germany (Go Local) | `disco.crm16.dynamics.com` | — |

And the geo code is not the same thing as the short name: `Oceania` carries geo `OCE`, `SouthAmerica` carries `LATAM`, and the two North America entries carry no geo code at all, so a lookup by geo will never find them.

The same region number appears in an organization's own hostname — `contoso.crm11.dynamics.com` is United Kingdom — which is how a client infers a region from a URL without asking anything. The rule is to drop the leftmost label, drop any `api` label, and match the remainder against the discovery hosts above.

tags.name: Environment Variables
tags.description: Environment variables: definitions, which ship inside solutions and carry a default, and values, which are the per-environment overrides. The mechanism by which one solution package behaves differently in dev, test and production.

tags.name: Fabric and Synapse Link
tags.description:
The Dataverse side of Link to Microsoft Fabric and Azure Synapse Link: the data-lake folder that anchors a link, the Synapse/Fabric database it feeds, the per-table sync state underneath it, and the per-table analytics opt-in that decides which tables take part.

None of it is created here. The orchestration service specified in [athena](spec:athena) writes these rows server-side when a link is created and removes them when it is destroyed; this surface is how a client observes and identifies them — in particular how it obtains the `datalakefolderid` that tearing a link down requires.

tags.name: Feature Control
tags.description: The per-environment feature switches — "feature control bits" — that gate platform behaviour independently of the `organization` row and of the backend settings beside it. Read-only from here: a switch is flipped by Microsoft, by the admin centre, or by a setting elsewhere, never by writing to this surface.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Resolving a bearer token to the Dataverse user, business unit and organization it maps to inside one environment.

tags.name: Organization Settings
tags.description: Environment-level configuration, which lives in three unrelated places: the very wide `organization` row, the weakly-typed OrgDB bag of backend feature switches beside it, and the `settingdefinitions` catalogue with its typed defaults. Beside the configuration surface sit the read-only functions by which an environment describes itself — its build, its instance type, its installed solutions, and the discovery record naming its own organization id and Power Platform environment id.

tags.name: Publishers
tags.description: Solution publishers — the identity that owns solutions and stamps its customization prefix onto every component they create.

tags.name: Records
tags.description: Generic record CRUD and OData query against any table, addressed by its collection name. One set of operations covers every table in the environment, custom ones included.

tags.name: Relationships
tags.description: Reading and changing the links between records: `@odata.bind` for single-valued lookups, and the `$ref` collection for collection-valued relationships such as a user's security roles.

tags.name: Solution Import
tags.description: Getting a solution package into an environment: staging and validating it, starting the import or in-place upgrade, polling the system job, and reading the verdict. Completion and success are deliberately separate questions here.

tags.name: Solutions
tags.description: The inventory of solutions installed in an environment, and their removal. A solution is the unit in which customizations are packaged and moved between environments.

tags.name: Table Definitions
tags.description: The metadata surface: the tables of an environment's model, their columns and their relationships. Reading only — authoring schema is outside this spec's scope. This is where a generic client learns the collection names, primary keys and navigation properties every other operation needs.

tags.name: Users and Roles
tags.description: Interactive and application users, the security roles granted to them, and the business units both are scoped to. Everything here is per environment: a user's identity, their roles, and the roles themselves all differ between environments.

servers.description: The Global Discovery Service. Unlike the rest of this spec it is not per environment — one host serves a whole cloud, and it is the service that tells a caller which environment hosts exist.

discoveryHost.description: Global discovery host for the cloud the identity lives in. `globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com` serves worldwide commercial. The others are separate services, not mirrors: a token for one is not accepted by another, and a commercial token sees nothing in a sovereign cloud. `globaldisco.crm9.dynamics.com` fronts the North America 2 scale group (US Gov community), `globaldisco.crm10.dynamics.com` and `globaldisco.crmtest.dynamics.com` are Microsoft's own pre-production and test rings and will not answer for a customer tenant. Sovereign clouds are inferred from the last three host labels: `crm.dynamics.cn` → China, `crm.microsoftdynamics.us` → US Gov High, `crm.appsplatform.us` → US Gov DoD, `crm9.dynamics.com` → US Gov, `crm10.dynamics.com` → pre-production, `crmtest.dynamics.com` → test, anything else ending `.dynamics.com` → commercial.

get.description:
Ask the service, without a token, which authority to authenticate against and which audience to ask that authority for.

This is how a client avoids hard-coding either. Send **no** `Authorization` header; the 401 that comes back carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer authorization_uri=…, resource_id=…`, and those two values are the whole answer. Build the scope from `resource_id`: `{resource_id}/user_impersonation` for a delegated sign-in, `{resource_id}.default` for a certificate or client-secret identity.

The dedicated path is not the only way to get the challenge — any unauthenticated request to the service produces the same header, so an unauthenticated `GET /api/discovery` on a discovery host, or `/api/data/v9.0` on an environment host, answers just as well. Use whichever is convenient.

Two details are worth handling deliberately. The advertised authority needs rewriting before use: strip the trailing `oauth2/authorize` and replace a `common` tenant segment with `organizations`. And only a 401 carries the challenge — **404 and 400 are failures**, not alternative sources for the header, so a request that lands on a path the service does not route is a dead end rather than a fallback.

401.description: The expected answer, and the point of the call. Both values live in `WWW-Authenticate`; a response missing either key is malformed, and there is nothing useful to retry.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer authorization_uri=…, resource_id=…`, comma-separated. `authorization_uri` is the Entra authority; `resource_id` is the audience, and is the service's own origin with a trailing slash.

post.description:
Sends several Web API requests in one round trip.

The body is a `multipart/mixed` document, **not JSON**: each part carries `Content-Type: application/http` and `Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary`, then a complete request line, its own headers, a blank line and its body. The boundary is chosen by the caller and named in the request's own `Content-Type`. Requests inside may use absolute URLs on this host. The response is `multipart/mixed` too.

Reads may be sent loose in the document as shown here. Writes that must succeed or fail together go inside a change set, which is a nested multipart part of its own; only change sets are transactional, a batch of loose requests is not.

x-notes.note: The response boundary is chosen by the service and has no relation to the request's. Parse it out of the response `Content-Type` rather than assuming symmetry.
A 200 on the batch says nothing about the requests inside it. Each part holds a full HTTP response, status line and headers included, so a part can fail while the batch succeeds.

schema.description: The batch document. Boundary lines, per-part headers and blank-line separators are significant; a missing blank line between a part's headers and its request line is the usual cause of a rejection.

200.description: The batch was parsed and each part attempted. **This says nothing about the parts** — read the status line inside each one. The boundary is the service's own, given in the response `Content-Type`.

post.description:
Evaluates one feature control bit for this environment.

It is an unbound **action**, not a function, so it is a POST with a JSON body even though it only reads — and it takes exactly one bit per call. There is no list form and no bulk form, which is why the admin centre's environment-settings page issues it dozens of times in a row to paint a single screen.

The bits are read-only from here. What flips one is a Microsoft release, an admin-centre toggle, or a setting on another surface; nothing in this spec writes them.

x-notes.note: The answer is a bare boolean with no error path. An unknown feature name, a feature that does not apply to this environment, and a feature that is switched off all answer `false` alike, so a name cannot be validated against this operation.

200.description: The bit's state. Answered for any name, including one that does not exist.

get.description:
Returns the solution new components land in when the caller does not name one.

An unbound function whose result is a single solution row — the context ends `#solutions/$entity`, so it is shaped like a record read rather than a function response, and `$expand=publisherid` works on it. Expanding the publisher is the usual reason to call it: the publisher's `customizationprefix` is what every component created without an explicit solution will be stamped with.

On an environment where nothing has been chosen this answers the Common Data Services Default Solution, whose id is the well-known constant below.

200.description: The preferred solution. `00000001-0000-0000-0001-00000000009b` is the default solution's fixed id, present on every environment.

post.description:
Reads the value of one namespaced feature control setting.

The sibling of `GetFeatureEnabledState` for settings that are not simply on or off: the name is scoped by an owning namespace and the value comes back as a string. Also an unbound action, so also a POST that only reads.

A namespace whose owning first-party component is not installed answers null rather than failing, so null is the ordinary response on a stock environment, not a signal that something went wrong.

200.description: The setting's value, or null when it has never been set here.

get.description:
Reads the *other* settings surface: the weakly-typed bag of feature switches — "OrgDB org settings" — that the organization row does not model as columns. Around 112 entries on a stock environment, and the set differs per environment and grows with each platform release.

Every value is a string; the entry's data type says how to read it. A setting absent from the list has never been set in this environment and is running on its server-side default, so absence is not the same as false.

This is a function result rather than a collection: no `value` array, no paging, and query options do not apply — the whole list comes back or none of it does.

200.description: Every backend setting that has a value in this environment. Settings never set are simply absent.

get.description:
Reads the verdict of an import job, keyed by the `ImportJobKey` the import or upgrade call returned. This — not the system job's status — is what decides whether an import succeeded.

Pinned to `v9.0` here; it answers identically under `v9.2` — the version segment is not load-bearing for this operation.

200.description: The import job's result. `SolutionOperationResult.Status` is the verdict; the message arrays carry the detail.

get.description:
Reports the Dataverse build serving this environment.

An unbound function, so a plain GET with no arguments. Environments in one tenant are upgraded on their own schedules, so this is a per-environment answer and not a tenant fact — the right check before relying on a feature whose availability is release-gated.

The build's major.minor is the platform version family, not the Web API version segment in the URL: an environment reporting `9.2.x` still routes `v9.0` and `v9.1` paths.

It is also the input to base-path construction: taking the result's major.minor as the version segment for every subsequent request makes a client's segment choice track the environment rather than the client. That is what makes it a natural first call after connecting.

post.description:
Writes one backend setting.

There is no batch form, so a caller changing several settings issues one request per setting and is not protected against a partial apply when a later one fails. `Value` is a string regardless of the setting's data type, but the service does type-check it against the setting's declared type before storing.

204.description: The setting is saved.

400.description: The write was refused: `0x81000067` when no setting exists with that name — names are case-sensitive and are not created on demand — or `0x81000068` when the value cannot be converted to the setting's declared data type. Both are client errors; do not retry.

500.description: An internal failure. Older platform builds report a refused setting this way rather than as a 400, so treat a 500 from this operation as a validation failure and surface the body rather than retrying.

get.description:
Reads one business unit.

Expanding `business_unit_roles` inlines the roles scoped to that unit, which is the direct way to enumerate the assignable roles for a user in it — roles are per unit, and a role from the wrong unit cannot be assigned.

The portal narrows that expansion with `$filter=issytemgenerated eq false` to hide the roles the platform generates for its own use. **Note the spelling**: the column is `issytemgenerated`, missing an `s`, and the misspelling is the real name.

Reads the environment's organization row.

There is exactly one, and it is the widest row on the API — 500 columns on a stock environment, holding audit configuration, attachment limits, IP firewall rules and feature toggles as ordinary columns. Always `$select`; reading it whole moves a great deal of data to answer a question about one flag.

`organizationid` from this row is the key the update needs, since the row cannot be patched through the collection.

200.description: A `value` array holding exactly one organization row.

patch.description:
Changes environment settings, one column at a time.

The row must be addressed by key; PATCH against the `organizations` collection is not allowed.

Send only the columns being changed.

Several settings interact: the audit sub-switches do nothing while the master switch is off, and the IP firewall's enforcing mode will lock out every caller including this one if the allowed range is wrong, so validate a range in audit mode first. Some columns are also one-way — `auditretentionperiodv2` cannot be set back to null once it holds a value; use `-1` (retain forever) instead.

x-notes.note: Read-only columns are accepted and silently discarded rather than refused. Patching `name` returns success and changes nothing, so a caller that round-trips the whole 500-column row gets a misleading success. Verify by reading back.
The 204 carries `Content-Type: text/html` despite the empty body, alongside a `Location` header naming the row.

204.description: Applied — but only for the columns that are writable. Read-only columns in the payload were discarded without comment, so success here does not prove the value changed.

Location.description: Absolute URL of the row that was patched, returned on a successful update as well as on a create. Redundant here — the caller already had the id.

400.description: The change was refused. A value outside a choice column's range reports `0x8004431a` and the message lists the accepted values; a column that cannot be null reports `0x80040200`; a property that is not on the type at all reports `0x80048d19`. Note that a merely *implausible* value in a writable numeric column is accepted rather than clamped.

500.description: An internal failure. Older platform builds report a rejected setting value this way rather than as a 400, so treat a 500 from this operation as a validation failure: surface the body rather than retrying.

get.description:
Lists user-to-role assignments as rows.

The queryable face of the same intersect table the `systemuserroles_association` `$ref` collection writes to, and the way to ask "does this user hold these particular roles" without expanding the user or walking the association. Both ends are plain columns rather than lookups, so they are filtered directly by name.

Guid comparisons here are **quoted** — `$filter=systemuserid eq '<guid>'` — the opposite of the unquoted form ordinary tables require on their `_..._value` shadows.

The rows carry only the two ids and the assignment's own key; there is no name and no expand path to one, so resolving a role name still needs the `roles` collection.

Reads a user by their Entra object id, addressed as an **alternate key** rather than by filtering.

`systemusers` declares `azureactivedirectoryobjectid` as an alternate key, so it can be written straight into the parentheses in place of the primary key. The guid goes in bare — `systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<guid>)` — with no quotes and no braces.

The difference from the equivalent `$filter` is the shape of the answer and of the failure: this returns the row itself with a `/$entity` context, and a 404 when there is no such user, where the filtered list returns an empty `value` array and a 200. For resolving one known person that is the more direct contract; for polling until a freshly granted user appears, the list form's 200-with-nothing is easier to loop on.

Without `$select` the whole row comes back — well over a hundred columns — so select what is needed.

404.description: No user in this environment carries that Entra object id. Expected for a person who has not been granted access, and also for one granted access seconds ago — the row lags the grant.

get.description:
Returns the privileges a user holds through the roles assigned to them directly.

A bound function, so the full namespaced name is appended to the user's URL and the result is a function response rather than a collection: no `value` array, no paging, no query options. On an administrator the set runs to several thousand entries in one body.

It answers what the user can do, not which roles say so — the roles are collapsed away, and privileges reaching them through team membership are **not** included. For those, use the through-teams variant beside this one and combine.

The portal sends `Consistency: Strong` on this call to avoid reading a stale replica after a role change.

Returns the privileges a user inherits from the teams they belong to.

The complement of the direct read, not a superset of it: a user in no role-bearing team gets an empty `RolePrivileges` array here while holding thousands directly. An empty result is therefore the normal answer and not a sign of a failed call. A caller wanting the effective set must union the two.

Both arguments are required — the function cannot be called bare — and both are written unquoted as `true`/`false` inside the parentheses. The portal sends `true` for both, which excludes privileges whose feature is switched off for the organization and applies setup-user filtering, so the answer reflects what the user can actually exercise.

200.description: Every team-inherited privilege. Empty when the user's teams hold no roles.

get.description:
Lists which users belong to which teams.

The second route by which a user acquires privileges: roles held by a team reach every member. A user audit that reads only `systemuserrolescollection` misses whatever their teams grant.

Every user belongs to at least their business unit's default team, so a non-empty result is the baseline rather than a signal. Guids are filtered unquoted here, unlike on `systemuserrolescollection`.

Lists the teams of this environment.

Expanding `teamroles_association` inlines the roles the team holds, which is what a caller needs to explain a privilege a user has but no direct role grants. That expansion is paged like the user one: a `teamroles_association@odata.nextLink` sibling of the inlined array means it was truncated, and it appears even when the array came back empty.

The collection accepts the `Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.In` function in place of a chain of `eq`s, which is how a caller asks for a known set of ids without building a long filter string. It works inside a `$batch` document as readily as on its own.

Lists the per-table analytics opt-ins.

`isenabledforadls` is the switch that decides whether a table takes part in data-lake export. A table with no row here has never been configured, which is not the same as being switched off — so a client cannot enumerate the excluded tables from this collection, only the considered ones.

A newly provisioned environment carries very few rows — often a single one, for an internal telemetry table.

200.description: The matching configurations. Sparse — absence of a row is the normal state for most tables.

get.description:
Lists the per-table sync state of a link.

One row per mirrored table, plus five rows for the metadata pseudo-tables the mirror also writes. Rows appear as the link initialises rather than all at once, so counting them against the table list is not a completeness test while a link is coming up.

`lakehouseshortcutstate` is the field that moves: 1 while the Fabric shortcut is being created, 3 once it is in place. `lastsynchronizedon`, `recordcount` and `sourcerecordcount` stay null even on finished rows, so they are not usable as progress signals.

Filter through the parent with `$filter=datalakefolder/datalakefolder_uniquename eq 'cds3_workspace'` and `$expand=datalakefolder` to get the folder alongside.

post.description:
Starts the asynchronous import of a package already staged.

Two correlation ids come back and both are needed: `AsyncOperationId` addresses the system job to poll for completion, and `ImportJobKey` addresses the import job whose result carries the actual verdict. Completion and success are separate questions — a job can complete having failed.

**Not idempotent.** A retry after an ambiguous transport failure starts a second import. Send it exactly once, then reconcile by polling.

`ComponentParameters` supplies deployment settings — connection references and environment variable values — each entry discriminated by an `@odata.type` naming the table it targets. Omit the property entirely rather than sending an empty array.

200.description: The import has been **started**, not completed. Poll the system job named by `AsyncOperationId`, then read the verdict with `ImportJobKey`.

400.description: The request was refused before any job started. An unknown or expired `StageSolutionUploadId` — including the all-zeros value a failed staging returns — reports `0x8004f066`.

post.description:
Promotes every unpublished customization in the environment to its published state. The body is an empty JSON object.

Synchronous from the caller's point of view — it hands back no async operation id — but on a large environment it runs for minutes and may time out at the gateway while the work continues server-side. It is safe to re-run, and a matching `PublishAll` system job is visible in `asyncoperations` while it runs.

204.description: Every pending customization is published.

get.description:
Resolves one setting for a scope, through the `settingdefinitions` catalogue rather than the OrgDB bag.

This is the third settings surface, and the newest: settings declared as rows in `settingdefinitions`, each with a type, a default and a scope at which it may be overridden. `AppUniqueName` selects that scope — a model-driven app's override, or the empty string for the organization-level value — and it must be present either way; the argument cannot be omitted.

Both arguments are string function arguments and are quoted inside the parentheses, unlike the guid arguments elsewhere in this spec.

The response carries the resolved value with its declared type, so unlike the OrgDB surface a caller can tell a real value from an absent one.

post.description:
The upgrade counterpart of the import call, taking the same request body and returning the same pair of correlation ids.

Where the import installs, this imports the package as a staged upgrade of an existing managed install and then applies it, deleting components the new version dropped. It requires the target solution to be already installed and managed.

Carries the same non-idempotency warning: send once, then poll.

200.description: The upgrade has been **started**, not completed. Poll as for an import.

post.description:
Uploads a base64-encoded solution `.zip` and validates it **without importing anything**.

On success `StageSolutionUploadId` is the handle passed to the import or upgrade call, and `SolutionDetails` reports the unique name, friendly name, version and managed flag read out of the package — the only way to learn what a package contains before committing to importing it.

Staging is idempotent and safe to repeat, each time yielding a fresh upload id. Uploads expire, so stage and import within the same run.

x-notes.note: A package that cannot be imported still returns a success status: the verdict is in `StageSolutionResults.StageSolutionStatus`, not in the status code. Only `Passed` means importable; `MissingDependencies` and `SolutionValidationResults` say why it is not.

The same relationship appears in `ManyToOneRelationships` of the referencing table and in `OneToManyRelationships` of the referenced table, so both carry `RelationshipType: OneToManyRelationship`.

get.description:
Traverses a collection-valued navigation property and returns the related rows themselves. `@odata.context` names the *related* table, not the one the traversal started from.

`$select` here is additive rather than exclusive: the related table's primary key and `@odata.etag` come back whether or not they were selected.

delete.description: The keyed alternative to removing through `$id`: the related record is addressed in the path instead of the query string. Identical in effect; both forms are accepted for collection-valued relationships.

204.description: Disassociated.

get.description: Returns entity references rather than rows: each entry is a lone `@odata.id` absolute URL. This is the cheap read for reconciling a desired relationship set against the current one — compare `@odata.id` strings, then add what is missing and remove the rest.

post.description:
Adds one entry to a collection-valued relationship. The body is a single `@odata.id` holding the **absolute** URL of the record to attach; a relative path is rejected outright rather than resolved against the request URL.

Adding a pair that is already related is accepted as a no-op, so a reconciling caller need not diff first — though it still should, to avoid the round trips.

204.description: Associated.

delete.description:
Removes one entry from a collection-valued relationship, naming the other end through the `$id` query parameter as an absolute URL. This is the form the security-role assignment surface uses.

A `$id` naming a record that does not exist is reported as a missing record, not as a missing relationship — the service resolves the target before checking whether the two are related.

204.description: Disassociated.

servers.description: The Global Discovery Service. Unlike the rest of this spec it is not per environment — one host serves a whole cloud, and it is the service that tells a caller which environment hosts exist.

discoveryHost.description: Global discovery host for the cloud the identity lives in. `globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com` serves worldwide commercial. The others are separate services, not mirrors: a token for one is not accepted by another, and a commercial token sees nothing in a sovereign cloud. `globaldisco.crm9.dynamics.com` fronts the North America 2 scale group (US Gov community), `globaldisco.crm10.dynamics.com` and `globaldisco.crmtest.dynamics.com` are Microsoft's own pre-production and test rings and will not answer for a customer tenant. Sovereign clouds are inferred from the last three host labels: `crm.dynamics.cn` → China, `crm.microsoftdynamics.us` → US Gov High, `crm.appsplatform.us` → US Gov DoD, `crm9.dynamics.com` → US Gov, `crm10.dynamics.com` → pre-production, `crmtest.dynamics.com` → test, anything else ending `.dynamics.com` → commercial.

get.description:
Every Dataverse organization the token's user can reach, across every region of this cloud at once — there is no per-region call to make and no paging to follow.

Each entry carries both `Url` (the model-driven app the user browses to) and `ApiUrl` (the host the API endpoints hang off). They are usually different hosts: `ApiUrl` carries an extra `api` label. Build the Web API base as `{ApiUrl}/api/data/v{major}.{minor}/` using the entry's own `Version` truncated to two parts — an organization reporting `9.2.…` gets `/api/data/v9.2/` — which is exactly how this spec's per-environment `servers` value is meant to be resolved.

The result is not filtered to healthy environments. Entries can arrive `State: 1` (disabled), with a malformed or empty `Url`, or with no `EnvironmentId` at all; drop those rows rather than surfacing them.

200.description: Every instance visible to the caller. An identity with access to nothing answers 200 with an empty `value`, not 404.

401.description: The token was rejected. Two very different causes share this status. Either the token is for the wrong audience — discovery's audience is the discovery host, not an environment — in which case `WWW-Authenticate` names the right one; or the identity is a **service principal**, which the Global Discovery Service does not admit at all. The CLI cannot distinguish them either: it treats a 401 on an app-only-capable profile as the second case and falls back to BAPI's environment list.

The others are separate services, not mirrors: a token for one is not accepted by another, and a commercial token sees nothing in a sovereign cloud. `globaldisco.crm9.dynamics.com` fronts the North America 2 scale group (US Gov community), `globaldisco.crm10.dynamics.com` and `globaldisco.crmtest.dynamics.com` are Microsoft's own pre-production and test rings and will not answer for a customer tenant. Sovereign clouds are inferred from the last three host labels: `crm.dynamics.cn` → China, `crm.microsoftdynamics.us` → US Gov High, `crm.appsplatform.us` → US Gov DoD, `crm9.dynamics.com` → US Gov, `crm10.dynamics.com` → pre-production, `crmtest.dynamics.com` → test, anything else ending `.dynamics.com` → commercial.

get.description:
One instance by organization id.

The route is declared alongside the collection URL. Because the collection returns every organization the caller can reach in a single unpaged call, a client that needs just one can equally filter that result client-side.

The response is a single `DiscoveryInstance`.

401.description: The token was rejected. Two very different causes share this status. Either the token is for the wrong audience — discovery's audience is the discovery host, not an environment — in which case `WWW-Authenticate` names the right one; or the identity is a **service principal**, which the Global Discovery Service does not admit at all. The CLI cannot distinguish them either: it treats a 401 on an app-only-capable profile as the second case and falls back to BAPI's environment list.

get.description:
Reports whether read auditing is active for this environment.

It sits beside the Web API on the same host and the same token, under `/api/nosql/` rather than `/api/data/{version}/`; there is no version segment, no envelope, and the body is the bare JSON literal `true` or `false` with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.

It is the effective answer, not the stored one: the `organization` row's `isreadauditenabled` says what was configured, while this reports whether the audit store is actually serving reads — which is also false while the master audit switch is off.

x-notes.note: Not an OData endpoint, despite sharing the Web API's host and token. There is no version segment, no envelope, and `OData-Version` is absent from the response, so an OData client library cannot be pointed at it.

200.description: Whether read auditing is active. A bare boolean literal, not an object.

get.description:
Reports whether Dataverse search has been provisioned for this environment.

Another non-OData sibling of the Web API on the same host and token, under its own `/api/search/v1.0/` prefix with its own version scheme — `v1.0`, unrelated to the `v9.x` of the data endpoints. The body wraps a single object in `value` rather than an array, and carries no `@odata.context`.

Switching search on is an admin-centre operation, not one of these; this reports the result, and `notprovisioned` is what a stock environment says.

entra_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The audience is the environment's own URL, so the scope is per environment — `https://{organizationHost}/.default`. A 401 advertises both the authority and the expected audience in its `WWW-Authenticate` header, which is the reliable way to discover them. Build the scope from that header's `resource_id` rather than from configuration; the suffix depends on the credential — `{resource_id}/user_impersonation` for a delegated sign-in, `{resource_id}.default` for a certificate or client-secret identity. The advertised authority needs rewriting before use: drop a trailing `oauth2/authorize` and replace a `common` tenant segment with `organizations`.

scopes.https://{organizationHost}/.default: Full access to one environment's Dataverse Web API as the signed-in user.

apiVersion.name: apiVersion
apiVersion.description:
Web API version segment. `v9.2` is current and what generic clients use; `v9.0` and `v9.1` remain routable and answer identically for the operations here — the segment selects the CSDL a client validates against, not different behaviour.

A client need not pin a segment. Taking the environment's own build — from `RetrieveVersion`, or from a discovery instance's `Version` — truncated to major.minor and composed as `{host}/api/data/v{major}.{minor}/` keeps the segment tracking the environment; `9.0` is a safe fallback when no version is to hand, and the Web API is not served at all below major version 8. Traffic built that way scatters across segments, because the segment echoes whatever each environment reported rather than a choice the caller made.

logicalName.name: logicalName
logicalName.description: Singular logical name of the table, always lower case. Not the collection name that record URLs use.

entitySetName.name: entitySetName
entitySetName.description: The table's `EntitySetName` / `LogicalCollectionName`, which is what the Web API routes on — not the singular logical name. Resolve one from the other through the table definitions when only the logical name is held.

recordId.name: recordId
recordId.description: Primary key of the record: a bare guid, without braces and without quotes.

relatedRecordId.name: relatedRecordId
relatedRecordId.description: Primary key of the record on the other end of the relationship.

navigationProperty.name: navigationProperty
navigationProperty.description: The relationship's navigation property as it appears in the table's relationship metadata — `ReferencedEntityNavigationPropertyName`, `ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName`, or `Entity1`/`Entity2NavigationPropertyName` for many-to-many. It is **not** the relationship's `SchemaName`, which frequently differs.

solutionId.name: solutionId
solutionId.description: Primary key of the solution. Regenerated when a solution is re-imported, so it is not stable across environments — `uniquename` is.

organizationId.name: organizationId
organizationId.description: From the organization row's `organizationid`; there is no other way to obtain it except `WhoAmI`.

asyncOperationId.name: asyncOperationId
asyncOperationId.description: The `AsyncOperationId` handed back when the long-running operation was started.

importJobId.name: importJobId
importJobId.description: The `ImportJobKey` returned when the import was started. Written unquoted inside the function's parentheses, unlike a string function argument.

select.name: $select
select.description: Comma-separated column logical names. Exclusive on record reads; on a navigation-property traversal it is additive, and the related table's primary key and `@odata.etag` come back regardless.

filter.name: $filter
filter.description: OData filter expression. Guid comparisons are written **unquoted**; string comparisons are quoted, with an embedded apostrophe escaped by doubling it. Lookup columns are filtered through their read-only `_{navProperty}_value` shadow, never through the navigation property itself.

top.name: $top
top.description: Maximum rows to return. Honoured on entity sets; **accepted and ignored on the `EntityDefinitions` metadata surface**, which always returns everything.

expand.name: $expand
expand.description: Navigation properties to inline, each optionally with its own nested `$select`. An expanded collection can itself be paged — a `{navProperty}@odata.nextLink` sibling of the inlined array means the expansion was truncated.

expandRelationships.name: $expand
expandRelationships.description: Relationship metadata collections to inline. Each is expensive: expanding all three on a stock table returns dozens of fully-detailed relationship objects.

expandOptionSet.name: $expand
expandOptionSet.description: Expand an attribute's option set. Only meaningful once the collection has been cast to a concrete metadata subtype that has one.

count.name: $count
count.description: Adds `@odata.count` to the response envelope. The count saturates at 5000 on large tables.

apply.name: $apply
apply.description: OData aggregation. Results arrive inside the ordinary `value` array, padded with null managed-property columns (`canbedeleted`, `iscustomizable`) that were never asked for.

savedQuery.name: savedQuery
savedQuery.description: Run a stored **system** view instead of an inline query. The view supplies the column list, which is reflected in `@odata.context`. Mutually exclusive with `userQuery`.

userQuery.name: userQuery
userQuery.description: Run a stored **personal** view. Mutually exclusive with `savedQuery`.

refId.name: $id
refId.description: Absolute URL of the record on the other end of the relationship. Must be absolute and on the same environment host.

preferHeader.name: Prefer
preferHeader.description:
OData preferences, comma-separated. Three matter on this API:

- `return=representation` — make a create or update answer with the affected row instead of an empty body.
- `odata.maxpagesize=N` — lower the 5000-row server-driven page size.
- `odata.include-annotations="…totalrecordcount,…totalrecordcountlimitexceeded"` — add the CRM count annotations to a collection response.

Whatever the service honoured is echoed back in `Preference-Applied`; anything it does not support is dropped without complaint.

`odata.include-annotations=*` is the blunt form of the third preference: it annotates every response rather than naming the annotations wanted, so annotations turn up on responses a caller did not specifically ask to annotate.

ifMatch.name: If-Match
ifMatch.description: `*` forbids the upsert-create on PATCH, making the request update-only. An etag value instead makes the write conditional on the row not having changed since it was read.

ifNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
ifNoneMatch.description: `*` forbids the update on PATCH, making the request create-only.

azureActiveDirectoryObjectId.name: azureActiveDirectoryObjectId
azureActiveDirectoryObjectId.description: Entra object id of an interactive user, used here as an **alternate key** rather than as a filter. Written bare inside the parentheses — no quotes and no braces — as `systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<guid>)`.

settingName.name: settingName
settingName.description: Case-sensitive name of the setting, quoted inside the function's parentheses.

appUniqueName.name: appUniqueName
appUniqueName.description: Unique name of the model-driven app whose override should be read, or the empty string for the organization-level value. Required even when empty — the argument cannot be omitted.

attributeLogicalName.name: attributeLogicalName
attributeLogicalName.description: Logical name of the column, always lower case. Platform columns are occasionally misspelled and the misspelling is the real name — `role` carries `issytemgenerated`, not `issystemgenerated`.

retrieveAllSettings.name: RetrieveAllSettings
retrieveAllSettings.description: Metadata-only query option, spelled in PascalCase and not an OData one. Returns the full property set of each table definition including the properties normally elided from a list, at a noticeable cost in response size.

excludeOrgDisabledPrivileges.name: ExcludeOrgDisabledPrivileges
excludeOrgDisabledPrivileges.description: Drop privileges whose underlying feature is switched off for the organization, so the result reflects what the user can actually do rather than what the role grants on paper.

includeSetupUserFiltering.name: IncludeSetupUserFiltering
includeSetupUserFiltering.description: Apply the filtering that hides privileges only a setup user holds.

discoveryVersion.name: discoveryVersion
discoveryVersion.description: Global discovery API version segment. Use `2.0`; version 1.0 was the preview generation and is superseded.

instanceId.name: instanceId
instanceId.description: The organization id — the `Id` of an instance from the collection, and the same value as `organizationid` inside that environment.

accessType.name: accessType
accessType.description: Which endpoint addresses to report. `Default` is what every online caller wants; `Internet` and `Intranet` distinguish the two published address sets an on-premises deployment can have, and are meaningless online.

mscrmSolutionUniqueName.name: MSCRM.SolutionUniqueName
mscrmSolutionUniqueName.description: Add whatever this request creates to the named solution, by unique name. Without it a newly created customizable component lands in the environment's default solution, which is the usual reason a component created by automation cannot later be exported.

mscrmBypassCustomPluginExecution.name: MSCRM.BypassCustomPluginExecution
mscrmBypassCustomPluginExecution.description: Skip custom (non-Microsoft) plug-ins and real-time workflows for this request. Intended for bulk data movement where business logic would be wrong or ruinously slow; it needs the `prvBypassCustomBusinessLogic` privilege, and it changes what the data means, so it is not a performance knob to reach for casually. Requires platform 9.1.0.20918 or later; below that build the header has no effect, so check the environment's version before relying on it.

mscrmSuppressDuplicateDetection.name: MSCRM.SuppressDuplicateDetection
mscrmSuppressDuplicateDetection.description: `false` runs duplicate-detection rules on this create or update and **fails the request** when one matches, rather than writing a duplicate. `true` suppresses them. Only meaningful where duplicate-detection rules are published for the table.

consistency.name: Consistency
consistency.description: `Strong` forces the request to see the server's current metadata rather than a cached copy. Worth sending on the read that immediately follows a schema change — without it a freshly created column or table can be invisible for a short while. Requires platform 9.1 or later.

mscrmCallerId.name: MSCRMCallerID
mscrmCallerId.description: Impersonate a Dataverse user, by `systemuserid`. The request executes with that user's privileges and ownership, and audit records name them rather than the authenticated identity. The authenticated caller needs the `prvActOnBehalfOfAnotherUser` privilege. Use `CallerObjectId` instead when what you hold is an Entra object id.

callerObjectId.name: CallerObjectId
callerObjectId.description: Impersonate a user by their **Entra object id** rather than their `systemuserid`, which saves resolving one to the other first. Same privilege requirement as `MSCRMCallerID`; send one or the other, not both. Requires platform 8.1 or later.

400.description: Bad request, and a client bug rather than a transient failure. An unknown column in `$select` or `$filter` reports `0x80060888`; a payload that will not deserialize — a missing action parameter, an undeclared property, a relative URI where an absolute one was required — reports `0x80048d19`; a missing required column or an all-zeros guid reports `0x80040203`; a value outside a choice column's range reports `0x8004431a` and the message lists the accepted values.

401.description: Unauthorized. The body is **empty** — the reason is in the headers. `WWW-Authenticate` names both the authority to authenticate against and the audience to request a token for, which is the environment's own URL.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer authorization_uri=…, resource_id=https://{host}/`. The `resource_id` is the scope to request.

401_error_reason.description: Non-standard Dataverse header spelling out the failure, e.g. a missing or malformed `Authorization` header.

403.description: Forbidden. The token is valid but the Dataverse user it maps to lacks the privilege for this operation — or has no user row in this environment at all, which is the usual cause for a service principal that was never registered as an application user.

404.description: Not found, reported as `0x80040217` when a record, function argument or reference target does not exist — the entity name and id are quoted in the message — and as `0x80060888` when a URL segment or property is not part of the model at all. Three cases surface here that a caller might expect elsewhere: a delete against a record that is already gone, a PATCH carrying `If-Match: *` against a record that does not exist, and an association whose target record does not exist.

405.description: The method is not allowed on this resource — most commonly a PATCH aimed at a collection rather than at a keyed record. The error envelope is present but its `code` is the **empty string**.

412.description: Precondition failed. `If-None-Match: *` against an existing record reports `0x80040237` ("a record with matching key values already exists"); a stale etag in `If-Match` reports `0x80060882`. Note that `If-Match: *` against a **missing** record answers 404 rather than 412.

429.description:
Throttled by service protection limits, which count requests, execution time and concurrency per user per environment over a rolling five-minute window. Because the limits are per user, fanning work out across records makes throttling **more** likely, not less. Honour `Retry-After` rather than backing off on a schedule of your own.

Three distinct codes share this status: `0x80072321` time-limit exceeded, `0x80072322` burst request-limit exceeded, and `0x80072326` concurrency-limit exceeded. Only the concurrency one is worth backing off exponentially on — the other two are windowed, so `Retry-After` is the real answer whenever the header is present.

Error bodies on this API spell `code` hexadecimally, but the same values also circulate as **signed decimal integers** — `0x80072322` is `-2147015902`. Match on both forms.

501.description: The `apiVersion` segment names a Web API version this environment does not serve, reported as `0x8006088a`. `v9.3` and above are not available.

ODataContext.description: Absolute URL of this environment's `$metadata` document with a fragment naming what came back: `#solutions` for a collection, `#solutions(publisherid())` when expanded, `#accounts(<id>)/$entity` for a single record, `#Collection($ref)` for a reference collection, and `#Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.<Name>Response` for a function or action result. Splitting the fragment at the first `(` or `/` yields the collection name the response came from, which is how a generic client recovers a table name it did not know.

ODataError.description: The error envelope of every Dataverse Web API failure that reaches the OData layer. Two failures do not use it: a 401, whose body is empty, and a request with no api-version segment, which answers with the pre-OData shape instead.

ODataErrorBody.description: The failure itself. Only `code` is worth matching on.

code.description:
Hexadecimal Dataverse status code, as a string. Stable across locales and platform versions, unlike the message, and the only part of the error worth matching on. Codes this surface returns:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x80040200` | A required column was set to null on update. |
| `0x80040203` | A required column was missing, or an argument was invalid — including an all-zeros guid. |
| `0x80040217` | The record, function argument or reference target does not exist. |
| `0x80040237` | A record with matching key values already exists. |
| `0x8004431a` | A value is outside a choice column's valid range; the message lists the accepted values. |
| `0x80044331` | A uniqueness constraint was violated, such as a duplicate publisher unique name. |
| `0x80048d19` | The request payload could not be deserialized — a missing action parameter, an undeclared property, or a relative URI where an absolute one was required. |
| `0x8004f066` | The staged solution upload id is not valid or has expired. |
| `0x80060882` | The etag in `If-Match` does not match the stored row version. |
| `0x80060888` | A URL segment, property or entity reference is not part of the model. |
| `0x8006088a` | The requested api-version is not served. |
| `0x81000067` | No backend setting exists with that name. |
| `0x81000068` | A backend setting value could not be converted to the setting's data type. |

Some transport-level failures — a method not allowed on a resource, for instance — return this envelope with `code` set to the **empty string**, so a client must tolerate that rather than assume a code is always present.

message.description: Human-readable, **localized**, and interpolated with entity names and ids. Never parse it; match on `code` instead.
message.example: Entity 'account' With Id = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 Does Not Exist

@Microsoft.PowerApps.CDS.ErrorDetails.Op.description: Present on some platform-level errors; carries a secondary status the plugin pipeline attached.

innererror.description: Present on unhandled server-side faults. Carries a stack trace in non-production configurations, so it should not be surfaced to end users.

NonODataError.description: The shape of failures rejected **before** the OData layer sees them — notably a request whose path carries no api-version segment. A client that unconditionally reads `error.code` finds nothing here.

Message.description: The whole failure. There is no code to match on.
Message.example: Requested API Version must be provided.  Please provide in the format /api/data/v<Major>.<Minor>/

WhoAmIResponse.description: The Dataverse identity a bearer token maps to in this environment.

UserId.description: The caller's `systemuserid` in this environment. A different guid from the Entra object id, and different again in every other environment.

BusinessUnitId.description: Business unit the caller's user row belongs to. Determines which security roles can be assigned to them.

OrganizationId.description: Identifies the environment's Dataverse organization. The key `organizations_update` needs.

EntityDefinition.description: One table's metadata. Around 115 properties without `$select`; listed here are the ones a generic client needs to build URLs and resolve relationships.

MetadataId.description: Identifies this metadata object, not the table's records.

LogicalName.description: Singular, always lower case. What callers usually hold.

SchemaName.description: Cased form of the logical name, used in solution component references.

LogicalCollectionName.description: Plural name. Equal to `EntitySetName` in practice.

EntitySetName.description: The OData entity set — **this is what routes record URLs**. Prefer it over `LogicalCollectionName` when they could differ.

PrimaryIdAttribute.description: Logical name of the primary key column. Needed to tell an update from a create when a caller supplies an untyped column map, since finding this column in the map means the record's identity is already known.

PrimaryNameAttribute.description: Logical name of the column used as the record's display label in lookups and views.

ObjectTypeCode.description: Legacy numeric entity type code. Still used by columns that store a table reference, such as `returnedtypecode` on a view.

OwnershipType.description: Who a record can belong to, which in turn determines which security-role privilege depths mean anything for this table.

TableType.description: Storage model. `Elastic` tables trade transactional guarantees and some OData constructs for scale; `Virtual` tables are backed by an external data source and are read-mostly.

IsCustomEntity.description: False on tables that ship with the platform.

IsManaged.description: True when the table arrived inside a managed solution and cannot be edited directly.

OneToManyRelationships.description: Present only under `$expand`. Relationships in which this table is the *referenced* (one) side.

ManyToOneRelationships.description: Present only under `$expand`. Relationships in which this table is the *referencing* (many) side. The same shape as `OneToManyRelationships`, down to carrying `RelationshipType: OneToManyRelationship`, because it is the same relationship seen from the other end.

ManyToManyRelationships.description: Present only under `$expand`. A different shape from the other two: symmetric Entity1/Entity2 naming rather than Referenced/Referencing.

EntityDefinitionCollection.description: A metadata collection. Unlike entity-set collections it carries no paging or count annotations, because the metadata surface never pages.

value.description: Every matching table definition.

Label.description: A localizable metadata label. Read `UserLocalizedLabel` in preference to indexing `LocalizedLabels`; it is the entry matching the caller's language, resolved server-side.

LocalizedLabels.description: One entry per language provisioned in the environment. Empty on labels that were never given text.

LocalizedLabel.description: One language's text for a metadata label.

Label.description: The text. Can legitimately be the empty string.

LanguageCode.description: Windows LCID, e.g. 1033 for English (United States).

IsManaged.description: True when the label arrived in a managed solution.

MetadataId.description: Identifies this label, so it can be patched independently of its parent.

AttributeMetadata.description: One column's metadata. Polymorphic on `@odata.type`; without `$select` each row carries around 55 properties, and casting the collection to a concrete subtype exposes the properties only that subtype has.

@odata.type.description: Names the concrete metadata subtype. **Absent** on rows of the plain base type — the shadow `…name` columns that accompany option sets, for instance — so a client cannot assume it is present. Fifteen distinct subtypes appear on a stock `account` table.

LogicalName.description: The column name used in record payloads and OData query options.

SchemaName.description: Cased form of the logical name.

AttributeType.description: The column's type, mirroring the `@odata.type` subtype but always present.

IsCustomAttribute.description: False on columns that ship with the platform.

IsValidForCreate.description: False on columns the service computes; sending one in a create is rejected.

IsValidForUpdate.description: False on write-once columns. Together with `IsValidForCreate` this is how a generic client decides what it may put in a payload.

IsValidForRead.description: False on columns that exist in the model but are never returned.

AttributeMetadataCollection.description: Every column of one table. Unpaged, like the rest of the metadata surface.

value.description: The table's columns, ordered by logical name.

OptionSetMetadata.description: The set of values a choice column accepts. Reached by casting the attribute to its concrete metadata subtype and expanding — the authoritative source for a column's real values, rather than inferring them from data.

Name.description: Set name. Publisher-prefixed on custom global option sets.

IsGlobal.description: True when the set is shared between columns, so editing it affects every column that uses it.

Options.description: The permitted values with their labels.

OptionMetadata.description: One permitted value of a choice column.

Value.description: The integer stored in the record. Custom values are allocated inside the publisher's reserved option-value range.

OneToManyRelationshipMetadata.description: A one-to-many relationship, described from whichever side was asked. Note the absence of `Entity1LogicalName`/`Entity2LogicalName`: those exist only on many-to-many metadata, so code that reads them off a one-to-many entry finds nothing.

SchemaName.description: The relationship's own name. **Not** what goes in a navigation-property URL segment — use the navigation property names below.

RelationshipType.description: Always this value on both `OneToManyRelationships` and `ManyToOneRelationships` entries, since they are the same relationship viewed from opposite ends.

ReferencedEntity.description: Logical name of the table on the *one* side — the target of the lookup.

ReferencedAttribute.description: Usually the referenced table's primary key.

ReferencingEntity.description: Logical name of the table on the *many* side — the one holding the lookup column.

ReferencingAttribute.description: The lookup column itself. Its read shadow is `_{this}_value`.

ReferencedEntityNavigationPropertyName.description: URL segment for traversing from the one side to the collection of many. This is what goes in a `$ref` path.

ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName.description: URL segment for traversing from the many side to the single one, and the property name to set with `@odata.bind`.

IsHierarchical.description: True on a self-referential relationship that forms a hierarchy, which unlocks the `Above`/`Under` filter operators.

Record.description:
A row of any table: column logical names mapped to values, plus the OData annotations the service adds.

Conventions that hold on every table:

- **Lookups read and write differently.** Reading gives the read-only shadow `_{navProperty}_value` holding a guid. Writing uses `{navProperty}@odata.bind` with a *relative* URL, where `{navProperty}` is the relationship's `ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName` — often cased and spelled differently from the column, so it must be read from metadata rather than derived. Writing the `_…_value` column directly is rejected.
- **Annotations arrive on request.** `Prefer: odata.include-annotations="*"` adds, per column: `{column}@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue` (the display string — a choice column's label, a money column's currency-formatted amount, a date in the caller's locale), and on lookups `_{nav}_value@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.lookuplogicalname` (the target table) and `_{nav}_value@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.associatednavigationproperty` (the navigation property to bind to, which is the reliable way to discover it inline).
- **Choice columns read as integers**, with the label only in the formatted-value annotation.
- **Selecting a money column silently pulls in `_transactioncurrencyid_value`** and its annotations, whether or not it was asked for.
- **Dates are UTC ISO-8601** ending in `Z`, except date-only columns, which are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **Money columns** are accompanied by a `{column}_base` in the organization's base currency, maintained by the service.
- Optional columns with no value are returned as explicit `null` rather than omitted.

plugintracelogsetting.description: How much plugin execution is written to the trace log: 0 Off, 1 Exception (only failed executions), 2 All. Anything but Off consumes storage, so All is a debugging setting rather than a steady state.

isreadauditenabled.description: Records read operations. By far the highest-volume audit category — enabling it on a busy environment generates a great deal of data. Requires the master switch.

auditretentionperiodv2.description: Days to retain audit records before the platform deletes them. `-1` means retain forever. Null until audit has ever been configured.

bounddashboarddefaultcardexpanded.description: Whether dashboard cards render expanded by default in model-driven apps.

iscustomcontrolsincanvasappsenabled.description: Allows Power Apps component framework components in canvas apps. Off by default because those components run with the app's privileges.

powerappsmakerbotenabled.description: Enables the Power Apps maker assistant for makers in this environment. **Null rather than false** when it has never been set, which is the state of a stock environment — so a client reading it as a boolean must treat null as "unset".

enableipbasedfirewallrule.description: **Enforcing** mode for the IP firewall: requests from outside the allowed ranges are refused. Turning this on with a wrong range locks out every caller including the one making the change — validate in audit mode first.

enableipbasedfirewallruleinauditmode.description: **Log-only** mode: out-of-range requests are logged but still served. The safe way to confirm an allow-list is complete before enforcing it.

allowediprangeforfirewall.description: Comma-separated CIDR ranges permitted when the firewall is on. Empty or null with enforcement on means nothing is permitted.

allowedservicetagsforfirewall.description: Comma-separated Azure service tags permitted alongside the IP ranges, for callers whose addresses are not stable.

allowmicrosofttrustedservicetags.description: Lets Microsoft's own trusted services through the firewall. Turning it off can break first-party integrations that have no fixed address.

allowapplicationuseraccess.description: Whether application users bypass the IP firewall. Service principals frequently call from addresses that cannot be enumerated, so switching this off tends to break automation before it stops an attacker.

enableipbasedcookiebinding.description: Binds a session cookie to the IP address it was issued to, so a stolen cookie is unusable elsewhere. Can disrupt users behind rotating egress addresses.

reverseproxyipaddresses.description: Addresses of trusted reverse proxies whose forwarded-for headers the firewall should believe instead of the connecting address.

aipromptsenabled.description: Enables AI prompt features for makers in this environment.

paipreviewscenarioenabled.description: Opts the environment into preview AI scenarios, which are not covered by the usual service commitments.

blockaccesstosessiontranscriptsforcopilo.description: Prevents makers and admins from reading Copilot Studio conversation transcripts, independently of whether transcripts are still being stored.

blocktranscriptrecordingforcopilotstudio.description: Stops Copilot Studio conversation transcripts being stored at all. Stronger than blocking access, and removes the data a maker would use to improve an agent.

enablecopilotstudiosharedatawithvivainsi.description: Shares Copilot Studio usage data with Viva Insights.

enablecopilotstudiocrossgeosharedatawith.description: Permits that sharing to cross a geographic boundary — a data-residency decision, not just a feature toggle.

suppressvalidationemails.description: Suppresses the notification emails the platform sends when solution-checker validation finds problems during a solution import. Set it when an automated pipeline imports frequently and the mail is noise; it does not change whether validation runs.

validationmode.description: How hard solution-checker validation is enforced on import. `0` is the stock value; the full value set is not documented.

releasechannel.description: Which release wave the environment's model-driven apps follow: 0 Semi-Annual (the default), against the earlier Monthly channel. Determines when new platform behaviour reaches this environment's users, which is why two environments in one tenant can disagree about a feature.

Case-sensitive name of the feature control bit. The namespace is open and grows every release, so this is not a closed set; an unrecognised name is answered `false` rather than refused, which means a typo is indistinguishable from a switched-off feature.

Two naming conventions coexist and neither is authoritative: the older bits are prefixed `FCB.` (occasionally `FCB_`), the newer ones are bare. Both forms are live on the same environment at once.

GetFeatureEnabledStateResponse.description: Whether the named feature control bit is on for this environment.

IsFeatureEnabled.description: True when the bit is on. **False conflates three states**: the bit is off, the bit does not apply to this environment, and the name does not exist. There is no error path, so a caller cannot distinguish them.

RetrieveFeatureControlSettingRequest.description: Names a feature control setting within one owning namespace. Unlike `GetFeatureEnabledState` this reads the setting's *value*, which need not be boolean.

RetrieveFeatureControlSettingResponse.description: The value of one feature control setting.

FeatureControlSetting.description: The setting's value as a string, or **null when nothing has been set** — which is the normal answer for a namespace whose owning component is not installed. Null is not an error and does not mean "off"; it means the component's own default applies.

DatalakeFolder.description:
A row of the `datalakefolders` table: one named folder in a data lake that Dataverse writes into, and the anchor a Link to Fabric or Azure Synapse Link hangs off.

**A stock organization already has ten or so of these before it has ever been linked to anything.** They are provisioned by first-party components — process advisor, skill mining, analytics, the smart data import service and others — and they are indistinguishable from a link's folder by row count alone. Identify the one wanted by `datalakefolder_uniquename`.

datalakefolderid.description: The id [athena](spec:athena)'s unlink operation takes in its path. It is not returned by the link-create call, so it must be read from here and persisted at create time.

datalakefolder_uniquename.description: The stable, unlocalised key of the folder and the only sound way to pick one out. `cds3_workspace` is the folder a current Link to Fabric uses; `cds2_workspace` is the older Synapse-era equivalent that persists alongside it. The rest name their owning first-party component.

name.description: Display name. Not unique and not a key — it often repeats the folder's unique name, but is free to differ from it entirely.

path.description: Folder path inside the container. A short mnemonic (`CDS`, `CDS2`, `CDS3`) on the platform folders, and a bare guid on the ones a first-party component provisioned for itself.

containerendpoint.description: ADLS Gen2 filesystem endpoint the folder lives under, in the Microsoft-managed storage account backing the environment. Null when the folder has no container of its own — which a linked folder can be, so its presence says nothing about whether a link exists.

extendedproperties.description: A **JSON document carried as a string** — parse it, do not read it as an object. The only key it carries is `IsActiveFabricProfile`, which is the closest thing to a positive signal that this folder is the one a live Link to Fabric is using. Folders that have never been part of a link carry null, or an empty `{}`.

cdmpath.description: Relative path of the Common Data Model manifest describing what is written into the folder.

deltaLakePath.description: Sub-path holding the Delta Lake form of the data, when the folder maintains one. **Camel-cased**, unlike every other column on the row.

isexternallake.description: True when the folder points at a customer-owned storage account rather than the Microsoft-managed one. False for stock folders and for Fabric-linked ones alike.

isexternallakereadonly.description: True when an external lake is attached for reading only, so Dataverse does not write into it.

iscustomercapacity.description: True when the storage consumed counts against the customer's own capacity rather than the platform's.

iscompliancelake.description: True on a folder provisioned for compliance export rather than for analytics.

compliancelakelocation.description: Region of the compliance lake, when there is one.

isdeepcopyenabled.description: True when the folder receives a full copy of each table rather than an incremental feed.

sharedforreadaccess.description: True when the folder is shared out for read access beyond the environment.

synchronizeschematosynapsedb.description: True when Dataverse schema changes are pushed into the Synapse/Fabric database. True on the folders that back a link, false on the component-owned ones.

synchronizeschematodataverse.description: The reverse direction — schema changes made in the lake reflected back into Dataverse. False by default.

readersecuritygroupid.description: Entra group granted read access to the folder's storage. Null unless the link was configured with one.

contributorsecuritygroupid.description: Entra group granted write access to the folder's storage.

tenant.description: Azure tenant of an external lake. Null for the managed one.

subscription.description: Azure subscription of an external lake. Null for the managed one.

resourcegroup.description: Azure resource group of an external lake. Null for the managed one.

owningappid.description: Entra application id of the first-party component that provisioned the folder. The platform folders share one id; a component-owned folder carries its own, which is a reliable way to tell them apart.

_parentfolderid_value.description: Not populated; the table is flat in practice.

statecode.description: 0 Active, 1 Inactive. Always 0 in practice, including folders belonging to links that have been torn down — so state does not distinguish a live link's folder from a dead one's.

ismanaged.description: True on the platform-provisioned folders. A folder created by a component that installed unmanaged is false, so this does not separate link folders from the rest.

componentstate.description: Solution component state: 0 Published, 1 Unpublished, 2 Deleted, 3 Deleted Unpublished.

overwritetime.description: `1900-01-01T00:00:00Z` when the row has never been overwritten by a solution import.

synapsedatabases.description: The Synapse/Fabric databases fed from this folder. Present only under `$expand`, and **empty on all but the linked folder** — which makes a non-empty array the most direct signal of which folder a live link uses.

synapselinkexternaltablestates.description: Per-table sync state under this folder. Present only under `$expand`; one row per mirrored table plus the metadata pseudo-tables.
