DiscoveryInstance.description:
One Dataverse organization as global discovery describes it: its identity, its state, its version, and the two URLs a client needs. This is the join between the Power Platform view of an environment (`EnvironmentId`) and the Dataverse view of an organization (`Id`, `UniqueName`).

No field is marked required: nothing here has been exercised against the live service, so optionality is unproven. The first-party clients defensively treat `Id`, `UniqueName`, `Url` and `EnvironmentId` as capable of arriving empty.

Id.description: The organization id. The same value as `organizationid` in that environment's `organizations` row, and as `OrganizationId` from `RetrieveCurrentOrganization` — not the Power Platform environment id, which is `EnvironmentId` below.

UniqueName.description: The organization's immutable unique name, an opaque `unq`-prefixed hexadecimal string for environments provisioned through Power Platform. Stable across renames, unlike `FriendlyName`, and the key to match on first when resolving an organization by name.

UrlName.description: The DNS label the organization occupies — the leftmost component of `Url`. Renaming an environment's URL changes this.

FriendlyName.description: Display name. Not unique, not stable, and sometimes blank — fall back to `UniqueName` when it is.

State.description: Lifecycle state, as an integer rather than a name: `0` enabled, `1` disabled. A disabled organization is still listed, and its endpoints still resolve, but it will not serve requests — filter on this before trying to connect.

Version.description: The full platform build of this organization, four parts. Truncate to major.minor to build the Web API base path. `8.0` is a safe fallback when the string will not parse; the Web API is not served at all below major version 8.

Url.description: The model-driven app URL a user browses to. This is the value the CLI surfaces as an environment's `environmentUrl`, and an entry whose `Url` is empty or unparsable is dropped rather than reported.

ApiUrl.description: The host the service endpoints hang off, which is **not** the same host as `Url`: it carries an extra `api` label, which has to be stripped back out before the hostname is matched against the region table in the Discovery tag. Compose `{ApiUrl}/api/data/v{major}.{minor}/` for the OData Web API this spec describes, or `{ApiUrl}/XRMServices/2011/Organization.svc` for the SOAP endpoint it does not.

LastUpdated.description: When the discovery record was last refreshed. Carried as a plain string rather than a typed date.

Region.description: Geo code, matching the Geo code column of the region map in this tag's description. Used as a fallback label when a client cannot infer the region from the hostname; note that the two North America entries carry no geo code, so a geo lookup will not resolve them.

OrganizationType.description: What kind of organization this is — a customer environment, a trial, a developer environment, a Teams environment, and so on. The value belongs to a closed 17-member enumeration and may appear as either the member name or its ordinal. The member names are listed on this property in declaration order; a member's position is its ordinal.

TenantId.description: Entra tenant that owns the organization.

EnvironmentId.description: The Power Platform environment id — the join key to [bapi](spec:bapi) and [ppapi](spec:ppapi), and the reason this endpoint is worth calling from an infrastructure client. It can be empty, and the CLI logs a warning and keeps going when it will not parse as an environment identifier, so do not assume every organization has one.

TrialExpirationDate.description: When a trial organization expires. Meaningless for non-trial types. It is a non-nullable date, so an absent value arrives as the zero date rather than as null.

Purpose.description: The environment's declared purpose, the free-text label set at provisioning time and shown in the admin centre. Carried through discovery unparsed.

SchemaType.description: The schema variant the organization runs — which first-party data model was provisioned into it.

OrganizationEndpointCollection.description:
The organization's published service addresses, keyed by endpoint kind. Three kinds exist: `OrganizationService` (the SOAP endpoint, `…/XRMServices/2011/Organization.svc`), `OrganizationDataService` (the OData Web API base, `…/api/data/v{major}.{minor}/`) and `WebApplication` (the model-driven app URL).

**How this serialises over the Web API is unresolved.** In the SOAP contract it is a keyed collection, and a keyed collection can render in JSON either as an object keyed by those names or as an array of key/value pairs. It is modelled here as the object form; confirm the shape before depending on it.

OrganizationDetail.description: An organization as the discovery contract describes it. The same object the SOAP discovery service returns, which is why its field names are PascalCase and differ from the `organizations` table's lower-case column names for the same facts.

OrganizationId.description: Organization id — `organizationid` in the `organizations` row, and `Id` in a discovery instance.

OrganizationVersion.description: The platform build, four parts — the same value `RetrieveVersion` returns.

EnvironmentId.description: Power Platform environment id, the join key to the admin APIs. Empty rather than absent when the organization has none.

DatacenterId.description: Identifies the datacentre hosting the organization. Opaque — not a documented identifier and not correlatable with an Azure region name.

Geo.description: Geo code, matching the region map in the Discovery tag's description.

UrlName.description: The DNS label the organization occupies.

UniqueName.description: Immutable unique name; stable across renames.

State.description: `Enabled` or `Disabled`. Note the difference from discovery's `Instances` collection, which reports the same fact as the integer `0`/`1` — the integer is the enumeration's ordinal, so `0` is `Enabled` and `1` is `Disabled`.

OrganizationType.description: Instance type. The same closed 17-member set as a discovery instance's `OrganizationType`; see that property for the member names.

RetrieveCurrentOrganizationResponse.description: Envelope for the current organization's detail.

OrganizationInstalledSolution.description: One installed solution as the organization-info contract reports it. A thinner projection than the `solutions` table's row: identity, version and publisher only, with no managed flag and no install timestamps. Read the `solutions` collection when those matter.

SolutionUniqueName.description: The name to pass to `ExportSolution` and to match on; unlike `FriendlyName` it is unique and stable.

PublisherIdName.description: The publisher's display name, denormalised into this record.

OrganizationInfo.description: What kind of environment this is, and what is installed in it.

InstanceType.description: The environment's type — the same closed 17-member set as a discovery instance's `OrganizationType`; see that property for the member names. This is the check to make before writing: a `Trial` or `Developer` environment is not a production one.

Solutions.description: Installed solutions. Declared optional in the contract, unlike `InstanceType`.

RetrieveOrganizationInfoResponse.description: Envelope for the organization info. Note the lower-case initial on the payload property.

ExportComponentDetail.description: One component to include in a partial export.

ComponentId.description: The component's own id in its own table — a `workflowid`, an `attributeid` and so on, not a `solutioncomponentid`.

ComponentType.description: Solution component type code — the same numeric taxonomy as `solutioncomponent.componenttype` (1 entity, 2 attribute, 29 workflow, and so on). Large and open-ended; read the environment's own option set rather than hard-coding it.

AddRequiredComponents.description: Pull in whatever this component depends on. Leaving it false produces a package that may not import into an environment lacking those dependencies.

ExportComponentsParams.description: Restricts the export to a named set of components rather than everything the solution contains.

ExportSolutionRequest.description:
Which solution to export, in which form, and which categories of environment setting to carry along with it.

No member is marked required in the schema, but `SolutionName` must nevertheless be supplied: the call cannot mean anything without it.

SolutionName.description: The solution's **unique name** — `uniquename` on the `solutions` row, not `friendlyname`.

Managed.description: Produce a managed package rather than an unmanaged one. Managed is what gets deployed to test and production, where its components are locked against direct edits; unmanaged is the development form. The choice is not reversible after import.

TargetVersion.description: Downgrade the package to be importable by an older platform build, by excluding components that build does not understand. Omit to target the exporting environment's own version.

ExportAutoNumberingSettings.description: Include this environment's auto-numbering settings in the package. Importing a package that carries them overwrites the target environment's, so leave it off unless moving settings is the point of the export.

ExportSolutionFile.description: The `.zip` package, base64-encoded. There is no streaming form and no separate download URL — the whole package is this string, so a large solution means a large response.
